hooks.command: f=$(jq -r ".tool_input.file_path // empty"); case "$f" in *.py) command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; out=$(cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0; ruff check "$f" 2>&1) || { printf "%s\n" "$out" >&2; exit 2; };; esac; exit 0

_note_deny_publishing: Everything that moves a published artifact is denied outright rather than gated behind `ask`: cosign sign, skopeo copy/delete, podman/buildah push, gh release, tag deletion, and force push. AGENTS.md section 0 rule 6 says registry tags and git history here are outward-facing and an agent proposes rather than does. `gh pr merge` and `gh workflow run` are on this list for the same reason and it is not obvious why: merging to main triggers build.yml, which builds, signs with this repo's key, and promotes to :latest, and a workflow_dispatch of build.yml defaults to promote_to_stable=true. Both are one command away from moving :latest, so neither is a prompt the maintainer should be able to click through while distracted.
_note_gh_api: gh api is in `ask`, never `allow`. Permission rules match by command prefix, and `gh api` switches to POST as soon as -f/-F is present and honours -X for any method. An allow rule such as Bash(gh api repos/:*) would therefore approve mutations, including the workflow-dispatch endpoint that gh workflow run is denied for.
_note_zpool: zpool is denied wholesale rather than by subcommand. This repository is about ZFS, so a pool is plausibly attached to whatever machine an agent is running on, and the read-only subcommands are not worth the risk of a prefix rule that also matches zpool destroy or zpool labelclear.
_note_hook: The PostToolUse hook runs ruff on any .py file just written, and exits 2 so the finding is fed back rather than merely printed. It no-ops when ruff is absent, so it never blocks work on a machine without it -- CI is where the lint is enforced, per .github/workflows/test.yml.
